tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

1	# kitty: shared trip expenses CLI — design
2	
3	## Intent
4	
5	A small command-line tool for one group trip: record who paid for what (in any
6	currency), record repayments, and at the end work out who owes whom and the
7	payments that square everyone up. Reporting output is JSON so it can be
8	scripted against.
9	
10	## Goals
11	
12	- `python3 -m kitty <command>` from the project folder; Python standard library only.
13	- Runs on the user's Python, **3.9.6** — no 3.10+ syntax (`match`, `X | Y` annotations at runtime, etc.).
14	- All state in `./kitty.json` (current working directory).
15	- Money is exact: `decimal.Decimal` everywhere, never floats.
16	- Balances always sum to exactly zero.
17	- Every user mistake prints an error to stderr and exits with status 1. No tracebacks.
18	
19	## Non-goals
20	
21	- Multiple trips per file, user accounts, sync, networking, live exchange rates.
22	- Editing expenses in place (remove and re-add instead).
23	- Removing payments (not requested; can be added later).
24	
25	## Anti-goals
26	
27	- Balances that change after the fact because a rate or the member list changed.
28	- Cents that go missing or appear from nowhere through rounding.
29	
30	## Approaches considered
31	
32	1. **argparse + Decimal + plain dicts in JSON, a few small modules** (chosen).
33	   Each expense stores its locked-in rate, its base amount and its per-person
34	   shares (in base cents), computed when it's recorded. All reports are simple
35	   sums over stored records.
36	2. **Dataclass domain model with (de)serialisation layer.** More code and
37	   ceremony for no benefit at this size.
38	3. **Append-only command log replayed to derive state.** Elegant but overkill;
39	   re-deriving splits on replay is exactly what anti-goal 1 warns against.
40	
41	The user handed the how to me; I chose 1.
42	
43	## Decided by the user
44	
45	- Commands, options and JSON output shapes exactly as in the original request
46	  (reproduced below).
47	- **Rates lock in at record time.** An expense or payment in currency X uses
48	  the rate for X current at the moment it's added; `rate set` later only
49	  affects new entries. Using a non-base currency with no rate set is an error.
50	  `rate set` for the base currency is an error.
51	- `rate set USD 0.92` means 1 USD = 0.92 base.
52	- `balances`: positive = owed money, negative = owes.
53	- `report` counts each person's *share* of expenses, not what they paid.
54	- Money printed as strings with two decimals, in base currency except an
55	  expense's own `amount`.
56	
57	## Commands
58	
59	| Command | Effect / output |
60	|---|---|
61	| `init CUR` | Create `kitty.json` with base currency CUR. Error if it already exists. |
62	| `member add NAME` | Add member. Error if duplicate. |
63	| `member remove NAME` | Remove member. Error if unknown or referenced (see below). |
64	| `member list` | `["Alice", "Bob"]` in the order added. |
65	| `expense add PAYER AMOUNT DESCRIPTION... [--among A,B \| --exact A=30,B=20 \| --shares A=2,B=1 \| --percent A=60,B=40] [--currency CUR] [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--category CAT]` | Records expense, prints the new ID (just the integer). |
66	| `expense list` | `[{"id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount", "currency", "base_amount", "category", "shares"}]` ordered by id. |
67	| `expense remove ID` | Remove. Error if no such ID. |
68	| `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT [--currency CUR] [--date D]` | Records repayment. Prints nothing. |
69	| `rate set CUR RATE` | Set/replace rate. Prints nothing. |
70	| `balances` | `{"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"}` |
71	| `settle` | `[{"from", "to", "amount"}]` |
72	| `history NAME` | `[{"date", "description", "change", "balance"}]` |
73	| `report` | `{"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}` |
74	| `export FILE` | CSV: `id,date,payer,description,amount,currency,category,base_amount`. |
75	
76	JSON is printed with `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False)` (default separators,
77	matching the examples), one document per command.
78	
79	## Data file
80	
81	```json
82	{
83	  "version": 1,
84	  "base": "EUR",
85	  "members": ["Alice", "Bob"],
86	  "rates": {"USD": "0.92"},
87	  "next_id": 2,
88	  "next_seq": 3,
89	  "expenses": [
90	    {"id": 1, "seq": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice",
91	     "description": "Dinner", "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD",
92	     "rate": "0.92", "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food",
93	     "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}
94	  ],
95	  "payments": [
96	    {"seq": 2, "date": "2026-07-15", "from": "Bob", "to": "Alice",
97	     "amount": "20.70", "currency": "EUR", "rate": "1", "base_amount": "20.70"}
98	  ]
99	}
100	```
101	
102	- All money/rates stored as strings to keep Decimal exactness.
103	- `next_id`: expense IDs are never reused after removal.
104	- `seq`: one counter shared by expenses and payments, used to order
105	  same-date entries in `history` by when they were recorded.
106	- Writes are atomic (write temp file in the same dir, then `os.replace`).
107	- Missing file → error "no kitty.json here; run `init` first". Unreadable or
108	  malformed file → error, exit 1.
109	
110	## Money rules
111	
112	- **Amounts**: a positive decimal with at most 2 decimal places
113	  (`45`, `45.5`, `45.50` OK; `0`, `-3`, `1.234`, `abc` are errors).
114	- **Rates**: a positive decimal, any precision.
115	- **Currency codes**: upper-cased on input, must be 3 letters A–Z. The base
116	  currency always has rate 1 and needs no `rate set`.
117	- **Base amount** = `amount × rate`, rounded to cents, ROUND_HALF_UP.
118	- **Splitting** (all four modes go through one function): convert the base
119	  amount to integer cents, give each participant a weight, allocate
120	  proportionally by the *largest remainder* method; ties go to whoever
121	  comes first in the member list. Shares always sum exactly to the base
122	  amount.
123	  - default: everyone currently a member, weight 1 each.
124	  - `--among A,B`: those people, weight 1 each.
125	  - `--exact A=30,B=20`: values are in the **expense's currency**, follow the
126	    amount rules, and must sum exactly to AMOUNT; they're used as weights
127	    (so with the base currency the shares equal the given values exactly).
128	  - `--shares A=2,B=1`: positive decimal weights.
129	  - `--percent A=60,B=40`: positive decimals that must sum to exactly 100.
130	  - Only one of the four split options at a time. Names must be current
131	    members; no duplicates; malformed `A=x` pairs are errors.
132	- **Payer** need not be among the people in the split.
133	- Shares are stored at record time, so adding a member later doesn't
134	  change old expenses.
135	
136	## Calculations
137	
138	- **Balance** of a person = Σ base_amount of expenses they paid − Σ their
139	  shares + Σ payments they made − Σ payments they received.
140	- `balances` lists every current member (in member order), including
141	  `"0.00"`. Never print `-0.00`.
142	- **settle**: greedy. Repeatedly pair the largest debtor with the largest
143	  creditor (ties by member order), pay the smaller of the two magnitudes,
144	  and repeat until all are zero. At most n−1 payments; `[]` when everyone is
145	  even.
146	- **history NAME**: every expense where NAME is the payer or has a share, and
147	  every payment from/to NAME, sorted by (date, seq). `change` is that entry's
148	  effect on NAME's balance; `balance` is the running total. Payment
149	  descriptions: `"Payment to Bob"` / `"Payment from Bob"`. Unknown member → error.
150	- **report**: `{category: {member: total share}}`. Categories sorted
151	  alphabetically; inside each, only members with a share in that category,
152	  in member order. Payments are ignored.
153	- **export**: header row, then one row per expense ordered by id; `amount`

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.
